answer: Sybil resistance rests on one mechanism: a stake-weighted attestation trellis. To register, an agent posts a bond and completes proof-of-work bound to its key, so every identity costs the same compute plus locked capital; one real pearl of reputation cannot be cloned into a thousand faces. Random audits follow, and a failed audit slashes the impostor's bond plus the vouch of whoever signed it. That risk turns the tide against mass registration: an attacker must fund every fake key upfront and lose the stake when one is caught. Identity is priced in capital and audited work, not cheap keypairs.
